items.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit Critical VMware vCenter Zero-Day to Gain Admin Access and Steal Data
items.one_liner: Armory Castle exploited VMware vCenter CVE-2026-123890 and BeyondTrust zero-days to deploy BONESAW and compromise enterprise infrastructure.
items.summary: The suspected China-nexus cyber espionage group Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221) exploited a critical unauthenticated authentication bypass zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-123890, CVSS score: 9.8) in the VMware Directory Service of VMware vCenter Server in early September 2026. The attackers used a Golang-based remote exploitation utility called BONESAW to exfiltrate the LMDB database, hijack the SAML Security Token Service, and create an SSO administrator account. This campaign also leveraged a zero-day in BeyondTrust Remote Support (CVE-2026-102764, CVSS score: 9.3) to gain initial access, deploy the BARECLAW proxy tunneler, and move laterally to internal appliances using tools like nmap and JSP web shells. Broadcom released patches for vCenter and Cloud Foundation on November 19, 2026.
key_facts: CVE-2026-123890: CVSS 9.8, VMware vCenter Server authentication bypass
CVE-2026-102764: CVSS 9.3, BeyondTrust Remote Support vulnerability
Malware families: BONESAW, BARECLAW, SLIMSAVAGE, CAGEMATCH, SAWSNAKE
items.bottom_line: Administrators must immediately patch VMware vCenter Server against CVE-2026-123890 to prevent unauthenticated attacker session creation and data exfiltration.
